answer: Each applicant registers one pigment-doped crystal oscillator: the pigment mix sets its base resonance, its serial is filed once, and the applicant posts a 70 bond. Its frequency wander stays inside its filed range; an auditor re-measures it with a crystal spectrometer within 0.5 percent; mismatch or a reused serial burns the bond. Tuning costs 30+2(k-1)^2 per crystal, so 1000 fakes pay 665,697,000 plus 70,000 locked bonds as bands narrow and pigment costs rise. A rented-crystal ring fails: its wander never matches under a second key. An honest agent pays 30 once.
